title: personal-kpi-weekly-checkin-kai-nakamura-2026-04-01
content:
WIP weekly check-in notes - Kai
Date: 2026-04-01
Context: quick personal check-in for OKR progress and KPI numbers for the serving runtime team. Mostly notes to self + short action items.

Summary this week:
- Focused on rollout of batching heuristic v2 to reduce small-request tail latency and improve throughput for medium sequences. Canary ran on 3 nodes.
- Observed p95 token latency for chat-short workload drop from ~150ms to ~128ms in canary. Still seeing a small regresssion on p99 for batch size 1 requests.
- Cost-per-token (hosted test env) estimated improvement ~4% so far (need more stable numbers after 24h).
- Worked with Maya on the quantization pipeline fixes (PR #412) and ran local evals against curated prompt set.

KPI / OKR mapping:
- OKR 1.1 (Reduce tail latency): target p95 <= 120ms for chat-short by EOW Q2. Current p95 (canary): 128ms. Delta: 8ms.
- OKR 1.2 (Cost efficiency): target -10% cost/token vs baseline. Current estimate: -4% in canary. Need full rollout + cache improvements.
- Personal KR: ship batching heuristic v2 and follow-up mitigations for single-request p99 regressions.

Concrete metrics (canary env, 2026-03-30 snapshot):
- chat-short p50: 38ms
- chat-short p95: 128ms
- chat-short p99: 270ms (regression from 240ms baseline)
- throughput (tokens/s per GPU): +7% vs baseline
- estimated cost/token: -4%

What went well:
- Canary rollout was straightforward, autoscaler behaved as expected (no flapping).
- Maya's quantization fix reduced memory pressure on KV cache which helped throughput.
- Logging hooks allowed quick rollback when p99 spiked on one region.

Open / blockers:
- p99 single-request regressions need root cause. Hypothesis: batching heuristic adds small overhead path for batch size 1 in certain code path (lock contention or extra memcpy). Need flamegraphs.
- Need longer collection window for cost estimates; 24h is noisy. Ask infra to extend canary to 72h for cost analysis.
- Some test prompts in eval set are unstable (non-deterministic model outputs) - may need to exclude those for perf gating.

Action items (owner) - short list:
- Kai: run perf flamegraphs on canary nodes and isolate where batch=1 path diverges (due 2026-04-03).
- Maya: follow up on quantization PR behavior on 8-bit vs 4-bit on mem pressure; add unit test for KV cache mem accounting (due 2026-04-04).
- Hunter: extend canary window to 72h and add cost-aggregation job (JIRA-987) (due 2026-04-02).
- Kai + Maya: add a small synthetic test for single-request latency to CI (opt-in nightly) to catch regressions earlier.

Notes to self / thinking out loud:
- If p99 regression remains after flamegraphs, consider fallback rule: for batch size 1 route to optimized single-request kernel compiled variant. Add as canary feature flag first.
- Might be worth testing the batching heuristic with a tiny 'early-exit' for batch=1 that avoids extra memcpy - could be cheap and reduce p99.
- Re: cost: batching + prefix caching are orthogonal; unlocking both will hit cost target faster. Coordinate with cache team to prioritize prefix KVC improvements (Maya to sync).

Quick links / refs:
- Confluence: CON-1234 (batching heuristic design doc)
- JIRA: JIRA-987 (canary rollout and cost metrics)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412

TODOs for next check-in:
- Confirm p95 below 125ms across 3 regions or escalate to infra for deeper analysis.
- Validate cost savings after 72h canary (Hunter owning).
- Add CI synthetic for single-request p99 detection.

Random notes / scratch (keep here):
- Quick microbench command used: ./tools/perf-run --workload chat-short --nodes 3 --batching v2 --collect 2026-03-30
- Observed one noisy host with thermal throttling during run - filter hosts when aggregating (might explain p99 spike).

End of check-in.
